featured.title: Hinted Scaling Laws
featured.tldr: Giving models partial reference solutions turns a hard benchmark into a smooth family of easier ones, letting scaling laws fit on small, near-zero-accuracy models forecast large-model benchmark accuracy with far lower error.

featured.title: Rewriting Scaling Laws for Synthetic Data with Compute and Data Constraints
featured.tldr: A scaling law that charges for the compute spent generating synthetic rewrites predicts how much of a pretraining corpus should be rewritten, and shows that models trained on rewrites can beat the rewriter.

featured.title: How Far Are We from Removing the Visual Encoder? Scaling Laws for Encoder-Free Multimodal Pretraining
featured.tldr: A controlled scaling study finds encoder-free multimodal models trail encoder-based ones now but improve faster, with a fitted crossover near 6e21 FLOPs, far below flagship training budgets.
